chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who is due three days of fasting in the month; is it permissible for him to delay them and fast them at the end of the month? He said, 'There is no harm.' I said, 'Should he fast them consecutively or separate them?' He said, 'He may do whichever he prefers: if he wishes, he fasts them consecutively, and if he wishes, he separates them.'
ai.seo_question: Can missed fasting days be made up at the end of the month, and must they be consecutive?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in making up missed Ramadan fasts, permitting them to be delayed until the end of the lunar month. The Imam further grants the individual discretion to fast the three days either consecutively or separately, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease (*taysir*) in fulfilling obligatory acts when specific constraints are not mandated by textual evidence.
